title: Sensing the Gut: Enteroendocrine Cells and Nutrient Signals

generated.pipeline: extract → Opus draft → Codex accuracy gate and fixes

cards.front: In mice, a non-neuronal gut epithelial cell can act as a {{c1::first-order sensory cell}}, turning a luminal nutrient signal into rapid excitation of a vagal afferent.
cards.back: It is the first cell in the sensory chain, not just a hormone source.
cards.quote: a non-neuronal gut epithelial cell can act as a first-order sensory cell

cards.front: Why does this lesson say that no single experiment establishes the gut-to-brain nutrient route in mice?
cards.back: Because the route is established only by linking evidence across cell, synapse, nerve and behaviour; each experiment tests one link.
cards.quote: The route is established only by linking evidence across cell, synapse, nerve and behaviour

cards.front: If a gut epithelial cell makes a fast synapse onto a vagal afferent, does that rule out hormonal gut-brain signalling?
cards.back: No. A synaptic route can exist beside hormonal signalling; the two are not alternatives.
cards.quote: A synaptic route can exist beside hormonal signalling.

cards.front: Enterochromaffin (EC) cells make more than {{c1::90}} percent of the body's serotonin yet are under 1 percent of intestinal epithelial cells.
cards.back: Rare cells with a large share of one transmitter.
cards.quote: cells make more than 90 percent of the body's serotonin yet are under 1 percent of intestinal epithelial cells
cards.section: First establish a sensory epithelial cell

cards.front: In mouse intestinal organoids (Bellono and colleagues, 2017), which chemosensory receptors did tagged EC cells express?
cards.back: TRPA1, acting as an irritant receptor, and the odorant receptor Olfr558 as a sensor of a microbial metabolite.
cards.quote: TRPA1 acted as an irritant receptor, and the odorant receptor Olfr558 as a sensor of a microbial metabolite
cards.section: First establish a sensory epithelial cell

cards.front: In an ex vivo mouse colon preparation, epithelial norepinephrine or isovalerate was applied and single mucosal afferent fibres were recorded, with the 5-HT3 antagonist alosetron added. What was seen, and what does it show?
cards.back: Both stimuli evoked firing and alosetron blocked it. An EC-cell output drives a nerve through 5-HT3 receptors, as taste cells drive nerves.
cards.quote: epithelial norepinephrine or isovalerate evoked firing in single mucosal afferent fibres, and the 5-HT3 antagonist alosetron blocked it
cards.section: First establish a sensory epithelial cell

cards.front: A student reads that ex vivo colonic mucosal fibres fired to epithelial stimuli and that alosetron blocked it, and concludes that EC cells synapse onto the vagus. What is wrong, and why?
cards.back: The conclusion overreaches. The recorded fibres were pelvic, hence spinal, afferents; none was shown to be vagal. The result supports a sensory epithelial cell with an output onto a nerve, not a vagal synapse.
cards.quote: The recorded fibres were pelvic, hence spinal, afferents; none was shown to be vagal.
cards.section: First establish a sensory epithelial cell

cards.front: How did Bellono and colleagues describe the contacts between 5-HT3-receptor fibres and EC cells?
cards.back: As synaptic-like contacts. The hedge matters: structure resembling a synapse is not a demonstrated synapse.
cards.quote: Fibres carrying 5-HT3 receptors made what the authors called synaptic-like contacts with them.
cards.section: First establish a sensory epithelial cell

cards.front: What was the prevailing view of gut-to-brain sensing before 2018, as Kaelberer and colleagues put it?
cards.back: That the brain senses gut stimuli only through passive hormone release.
cards.quote: the brain senses gut stimuli only through passive hormone release

cards.front: Bohorquez and colleagues (2015) showed that a cytoplasmic process on enteroendocrine cells, earlier called a {{c1::neuropod}}, contacts mucosal nerves.
cards.back: Kaelberer and colleagues then asked whether that contact is a synapse, and called synaptically connected cells neuropod cells.
cards.quote: a cytoplasmic process on enteroendocrine cells, earlier called a neuropod, contacts mucosal nerves

cards.front: Modified rabies virus was given by enema to PYY-Cre pups or by gavage to CCK-Cre pups. In the colon experiment, what was found, and what claim does it earn?
cards.back: Labelling reached vagal nodose neurons in 2 of 5 mice with infected colon nerves. It earns a connection in some animals; tracing identifies neither the transmitter nor any behavioural role.
cards.quote: labelling reached vagal nodose neurons in 2 of 5 mice with infected colon nerves using the pseudotyped virus

cards.front: Enteroendocrine cells were found to express VGLUT1 transcripts. What does that observation earn, and what does it not?
cards.back: It fits glutamate release but does not show a postsynaptic effect; transcript alone is machinery, not transmission.
cards.quote: This fits glutamate release but does not show a postsynaptic effect.

cards.front: In cocultured enteroendocrine-cell and nodose-neuron pairs, how fast were the light-evoked excitatory postsynaptic currents?
cards.back: Within 60 to 800 ms of stimulating the gut cell, in 9 pairs.
cards.quote: light activation evoked excitatory postsynaptic currents within 60 to 800 ms

cards.front: In the coculture, kynurenic acid at 3 mM was applied and then washed out. What happened, and why is the washout step necessary?
cards.back: The currents were abolished and returned in 4 neurons on washout. The block shows ionotropic glutamate receptors carry the current; recovery argues the cells were not simply damaged.
cards.quote: Kynurenic acid at 3 mM, an ionotropic glutamate-receptor blocker, abolished the currents; washout restored them in 4 neurons.

cards.front: In anaesthetised mice, intestinal sucrose was given while the cervical vagus was recorded, with the SGLT1 blocker phloridzin, halorhodopsin silencing of CCK-labelled cells and channelrhodopsin activation. What was the result, and what did the authors conclude?
cards.back: Firing rose within seconds and peaked about a minute or more later; phloridzin and silencing abolished it, and activation raised firing. The authors concluded these cells were necessary and sufficient to transduce glucose in this preparation.
cards.why: Firing within seconds alone could still fit a hormone or a synapse.
cards.quote: intestinal sucrose raised cervical-vagus firing within seconds and peaked about a minute or more later

cards.front: A contact fraction of 18.9 percent was measured from more than 100 CCK-labelled cells per mouse in 3 mice. Which is the biological replicate, the cell or the mouse, and why?
cards.back: The mouse. Cells from one mouse are nested observations, not independent animals, so n is 3.
cards.quote: Cells sampled from the same mouse are nested observations, not independent animals.

cards.front: Latencies of 60 to 800 ms in coculture, vagal firing within seconds in vivo, and a preference emerging over 24 to 48 hours: can these be chained into one timescale for the route? Explain.
cards.back: No. They measure different processes, a synapse, an afferent response and learning, so they cannot be merged into a single latency.
cards.quote: Coculture latency in milliseconds, in-vivo firing within seconds and learned preference over 24 to 48 hours measure different processes.

cards.front: Why does a Cre-driver line not give a pure population of one mature gut cell type?
cards.back: It marks every cell that expressed the driver at some time, so the labelled set can include cells of other mature identities.
cards.quote: a Cre line is not pure by mature cell type because it marks cells that expressed the driver at some time

cards.front: Mice lacking T1R2/T1R3 (n = 5) or TRPM5 (n = 7) were offered sugar against acesulfame K at an equally attractive concentration for 48 hours. What happened, and what does it show?
cards.back: They still developed the sugar preference. Learned preference in this assay does not require sweet-taste signalling.
cards.quote: Mice lacking T1R2/T1R3 (n = 5) or TRPM5 (n = 7), which cannot taste sweetness, still developed the preference.
cards.section: Sugar without taste: locate each link

cards.front: In Tan and colleagues' two-bottle sugar-against-sweetener assay in mice, how fast did preference change?
cards.back: It shifted within 24 hours, and by 48 hours mice drank almost exclusively sugar.
cards.quote: Preference shifted within 24 hours, and by 48 hours mice drank almost exclusively sugar.
cards.section: Sugar without taste: locate each link

cards.front: Vagal-ganglion imaging found neurons responding to gut-delivered sugar but not to sweeteners. What happened when phlorizin was given into the intestine, and what does that locate?
cards.back: Glucose responses were dramatically lost, locating the transducing step at intestinal SGLT1 rather than at a sweet receptor.
cards.quote: intestinal phlorizin caused a dramatic loss of glucose responses
cards.section: Sugar without taste: locate each link

cards.front: Transmitter release was silenced in sugar-activated neurons of the caudal nucleus of the solitary tract, labelled with the activity-dependent driver TRAP2 (n = 6). What was the behavioural result?
cards.back: Development of sugar preference was abolished, while innate attraction to sugar and sweeteners remained. Learning and first-sip attraction are separable.
cards.quote: abolished development of sugar preference without removing innate attraction to sugar or sweeteners
cards.section: Sugar without taste: locate each link

cards.front: In Buchanan and colleagues (2022), which transmitter did CCK-labelled duodenal neuropod cells use to the vagus for sugar, and which for sweetener?
cards.back: Glutamatergic transmission for sugar and purinergic transmission for sweetener.
cards.quote: They reported glutamatergic transmission to the vagus for sugar and purinergic transmission for sweetener.
cards.section: Sugar without taste: locate each link

cards.front: Of 132 CCK-GFP small-intestinal cells from 3 mice, 60.1 percent expressed only Slc5a1 (SGLT1), 19.6 percent SGLT1 and Tas1r3, 1.2 percent only T1R3 and 19.1 percent neither. What share carried SGLT1, and about how many cells is that?
cards.back: 60.1 + 19.6 = 79.7 percent carried SGLT1. 0.797 x 132 = 105.2, so about 105 of the 132 cells.
cards.why: Only 1.2 percent carried T1R3 without SGLT1, so the transducer is the transporter, not the sweet receptor.
cards.quote: Of 132 CCK-GFP small-intestinal cells from 3 mice, 60.1 percent expressed only Slc5a1, which encodes SGLT1
cards.section: Sugar without taste: locate each link

cards.front: In these mouse studies, which molecule transduces intestinal sugar for the vagal route, and which does not?
cards.back: Epithelial SGLT1 transduces it; a sweet receptor does not.
cards.quote: In these mouse studies the sugar transducer is epithelial SGLT1, not a sweet receptor.
cards.section: Sugar without taste: locate each link

cards.front: What is the only human result in this evidence chain for the epithelial-to-vagal synapse, and what may be claimed from it?
cards.back: Glutamate release from organoids of one donor. The authors say it suggests conservation; it is not human behaviour.
cards.quote: The only human result is glutamate release from organoids of one donor.
cards.section: Sugar without taste: locate each link

cards.front: Light activation of gut-innervating vagal neurons in adult male mice sustained self-stimulation, flavour and place preference and dopamine release, on the right side only. Does that show a nutrient normally recruits this route?
cards.back: No. The stimulus was light, not a nutrient, so the result shows the route can sustain reward, not which nutrient normally recruits it.
cards.quote: The result shows that this route can sustain reward, not which nutrient normally recruits it.
cards.section: Sugar without taste: locate each link

cards.front: TRPM5-mutant mice, blind to fat taste, were offered 1.5 percent Intralipid against 3 mM acesulfame K for 48 hours with lick counters. What happened?
cards.back: They still developed a strong preference for the fat, so learned fat preference in this assay does not need fat taste.
cards.quote: TRPM5-mutant mice, blind to fat taste, still developed a strong preference.

cards.front: Which two response classes did vagal imaging reveal in Li and colleagues (2022)?
cards.back: A general nutrient population answering sugar, fat and amino acids, plus a fat-only, TRPA1-expressing cluster.
cards.quote: Vagal imaging revealed a general nutrient population responding to sugar, fat and amino acids, plus a fat-only, TRPA1-expressing cluster.

cards.front: VIP vagal neurons were silenced in mice offered fat against a sweetener. What happened to learned preference, and what stayed intact?
cards.back: Nutrient preference was markedly impaired, while immediate attraction to sugar and fat was intact, again separating learning from attraction.
cards.quote: Silencing VIP vagal neurons markedly impaired nutrient preference while leaving immediate attraction to sugar and fat intact.

cards.front: In SGLT1-knockout mice no vagal neurons answered intestinal sugar while fat responses remained, and fat responses fell substantially only in GPR40/GPR120 double and CD36/GPR40/GPR120 triple knockouts. What is the most direct conclusion?
cards.back: Intestinal sugar and fat responses have separable receptor requirements: sugar responses require SGLT1, while substantially reducing fat responses required combined receptor knockouts.
cards.quote: In SGLT1-knockout mice no vagal neurons responded to intestinal sugar, while fat responses remained.

cards.front: A germline receptor knockout removes a vagal nutrient response. What may be concluded, and what may not?
cards.back: That the receptor is needed in the animal, not which cell needs it: the deletion is neither acute nor restricted to one cell type.
cards.quote: A germline deletion is neither acute nor restricted to one cell type

cards.front: In a one-hour choice between 300 mM sucrose and 15 mM sucralose under the same light, controls showed 90.8 percent sucrose preference and mice with halorhodopsin in CCK-labelled duodenal cells showed 58.9 percent. Chance is 50 percent. What fraction of the above-chance preference was lost?
cards.back: About 78 percent. Control advantage 90.8 - 50 = 40.8 points; silenced advantage 58.9 - 50 = 8.9 points; loss 31.9 points; 31.9 / 40.8 = 0.78.
cards.quote: The silenced advantage is 58.9 − 50 = 8.9 points.

cards.front: The duodenal glutamate-receptor-block group chose sucrose 44.0 percent of the time. Should it be compared with 50 percent chance, with the 90.8 percent silencing control, or with its own 82.4 percent vehicle control?
cards.back: Use its own 82.4 percent vehicle control. Chance shows only that 44.0 percent is 6.0 points below indifference, and 90.8 percent came from a separate cohort.
cards.quote: Use its own 82.4 percent vehicle control.

cards.front: Why is the fraction of preference lost not computed as 31.9 divided by 90.8?
cards.back: Dividing by 90.8 mixes the chance half of the choice with the above-chance preference; only the part above 50 percent can be lost.
cards.quote: Dividing by 90.8 would mix the chance half of the choice with the above-chance preference.

cards.front: Which alternative explanation is addressed by finding locomotion and 24-hour food and water intake unchanged in the silenced mice?
cards.back: Illness or reduced general drinking as the cause of the shift in choice.
cards.quote: Locomotion and 24-hour food and water intake were unchanged, arguing against malaise or reduced general drinking.

cards.front: The preference percentages are quoted to one decimal place with N of 4 to 8 per group. What caution follows?
cards.back: With such small groups the percentages carry wide uncertainty that the decimal arithmetic hides; treat the 78 percent as an estimate.
cards.quote: With N of 4 to 8, the percentages carry wide uncertainty that the arithmetic hides.

cards.front: Across 9 ganglia, 60 of 203 VIP vagal neurons answered nutrients, and about 4 percent of all 203 were fat-only. What share of the nutrient-responsive group was fat-only?
cards.back: 60 / 203 = 29.6 percent responded, about 30 percent. 0.04 x 203 = about 8 neurons, and 8 / 60 = about 13 percent of the responsive group.
cards.why: The rest are broad responders that also answer sugar and amino acids.
cards.quote: Across 9 ganglia, 60 of 203 VIP neurons responded to nutrients

cards.front: The name GLP-1 appears in three places in this rodent evidence. Name the three lanes.
cards.back: Peripheral peptide from enteroendocrine L cells in the gut; central peptide from preproglucagon neurons in the brainstem; and vagal afferents defined by the GLP1R receptor.
cards.quote: The name GLP-1 appears in three different places.
cards.section: GLP-1: three routes, not one relay

cards.front: A student proposes: gut L-cell GLP-1 to vagal GLP1R neuron to brainstem PPG neuron, and eating falls. Which observations break this chain?
cards.back: Brainstem PPG neurons take vagal input predominantly from oxytocin-receptor neurons rather than GLP1R neurons, and they are not necessary for eating suppression by GLP-1 receptor agonists in mice. The last two links fail.
cards.why: The evidence supports several GLP-1-related routes, not one serial relay.
cards.quote: Brainstem PPG neurons receive vagal input predominantly from oxytocin-receptor neurons rather than GLP1R neurons
cards.section: GLP-1: three routes, not one relay

cards.front: GPR65 vagal neurons supply most intestinal villi. How did they respond to GLP-1 or cholecystokinin?
cards.back: They were insensitive to both, so dense villous supply does not by itself mean hormone sensitivity.
cards.quote: GPR65 neurons supply most villi but were insensitive to GLP-1 or cholecystokinin.
cards.section: GLP-1: three routes, not one relay

cards.front: Over 95 percent of GLP1R vagal neurons and over 97 percent of GPR65 neurons were slow {{c1::C}} fibres.
cards.quote: Over 95 percent of GLP1R neurons and over 97 percent of GPR65 neurons were slow C fibres.
cards.section: GLP-1: three routes, not one relay

cards.front: For one nutrient, design the test that decides whether the gut's message to the vagus is hormonal or synaptic.
cards.back: Look for a vesicular-transporter transcript in the cell; record a fast current with measured latency in coculture; block it with an ionotropic glutamate-receptor antagonist and show recovery on washout; then silence the cells to test necessity and drive them for sufficiency.
cards.quote: Record a fast current with measured latency in a coculture, block it with an ionotropic glutamate-receptor antagonist and show recovery on washout.

cards.front: Which two behavioural controls must a gut-nutrient preference experiment carry before its shift in choice counts as nutrient learning?
cards.back: A malaise control, and a separation of innate attraction from learned preference.
cards.quote: Include a malaise control and separate innate attraction from learned preference.

cards.front: What did Bayrer and colleagues (2023) report when EC-cell function was enhanced in mice?
cards.back: It was sufficient to cause hypersensitivity to gut distension; EC-cell activity was also necessary for the sensitising action of isovalerate.
cards.quote: enhancing EC-cell function was sufficient to cause hypersensitivity to gut distension in mice
cards.section: Enterochromaffin cells in an intact mouse

cards.front: GLP1R was deleted from glutamatergic (vGlut2) or from GABAergic (vGAT) neurons in mice given liraglutide. What were the results?
cards.back: Deletion from vGlut2 neurons eliminated the weight effect; deletion from vGAT neurons did not. In this mouse experiment, the weight effect required GLP1R in vGlut2-labelled neurons but not vGAT-labelled neurons.
cards.quote: Deleting GLP1R from glutamatergic, vGlut2, neurons eliminated liraglutide's weight effect, while deletion from GABAergic, vGAT, neurons did not
cards.section: GLP-1 drugs do not identify one physiological route

cards.front: In rats, vagal deafferentation did not block the 14-day weight effect of a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist. Why does that not mean vagal GLP-1 receptors are physiologically idle?
cards.back: Knockdown in rat nodose neurons enlarged meals, sped gastric emptying and raised postmeal glucose, with normal long-term energy balance. Thus vagal GLP-1 receptors still have physiological roles despite that specific drug result.
cards.quote: knockdown in rat nodose neurons enlarged meals, sped gastric emptying and raised postmeal glucose, with normal long-term energy balance
cards.section: GLP-1 drugs do not identify one physiological route

cards.front: After intravenous GLP-1(7-36) amide in 8 normal subjects, intact peptide was 19.9 percent of the rise in immunoreactivity on a COOH-terminal assay. What does this one human number let you say about the gut-brain route in people?
cards.back: Almost nothing about the route: it is a pharmacokinetic measurement showing most of the immunoreactive signal was not intact peptide. All route evidence here is rodent.
cards.quote: intact peptide was 19.9 percent of the rise in immunoreactivity measured with a COOH-terminal assay
cards.section: GLP-1 drugs do not identify one physiological route
